newsitem.title: USA: IBM slips as Q3 EPS comes in on target.
newsitem.headline: IBM slips as Q3 EPS comes in on target.

text.p: Shares of International Business Machines Corp slipped in early morning trading after the computer giant's third quarter earnings were only two cents above the consensus estimate, with no upside surprise.
IBM reported third quarter earnings of $1.3 billion, or $2.45 a share, two cents above the consensus estimate of $2.43 a share, according to First Call.

"The problem is, it's not blow-out numbers," said one trader. "There is nothing out that's going to make you jump out and buy IBM." Traders and analysts said that investors were awaiting IBM's analyst meeting/conference call at 1030.
Traders pointed out that IBM shares surged over three to 129-3/8 in very active trading on Friday in anticipation of a strong third quarter.

"My initial read is that it's a great quarter," said David Takata, a Gruntal & Co analyst, but he added that he wanted to wait to make more comments until after IBM's chief financial officer G. Richard Thoman meets with analysts.
IBM shares were off 5/8 to 128-3/4 in active trading.
One trader said that some investors were speculating that IBM took a bigger-than-expected restructuring cost in the quarter, which is no longer counted as a restructuring charge.
